extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and other practitioners who practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO); patent practitioners and law firms advising on USPTO ethics and professional responsibilities
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the USPTO proposed Rules of Professional Conduct (sections 11.101–11.904 area) describing ethical, procedural, and recordkeeping duties for practitioners before the USPTO, including differences from ABA Model Rules and USPTO-specific provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client trust account recordkeeping and electronic records (§ 11.115(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must maintain the same records required by 37 CFR 10.112(c)(3) including complete records of all funds, securities and other properties of a client coming into the practitioner's possession; may maintain records in electronic, photographic, computer or other media or paper format, either at the practitioner's office or off-site, but off-site records must be readily accessible and producible/printable upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses Check 21 Act and increasing electronic transfers; clarifies recordkeeping after electronic transfers, who can authorize transfers, required safeguards for electronic storage systems, minimum safeguards when non-practitioner employees access client trust accounts, partner responsibilities for storage/access on dissolution or sale. Examples of required instruments include cash receipts/disbursements journals, subsidiary ledger, periodic trial balances, and insufficient fund check reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of complete client funds records (37 CFR 10.112(c)(3) standard carried forward)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to maintain complete records of all funds, securities and other properties of a client coming into the practitioner's possession (cash receipts journal, cash disbursements journal, subsidiary ledger, periodic trial balances, insufficient fund check reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.115(f) clarifies that practitioners must keep these traditional accounting and trust records; cites case law recognizing these obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties in declining or terminating representation (§ 11.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule providing practitioner responsibilities when declining or terminating representation of a client, corresponding to ABA Model Rule 1.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets forth obligations on withdrawal/termination consistent with client protection and case management; aligns USPTO practice with MRPC 1.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buying or selling a law practice (§ 11.117)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regarding responsibilities when buying or selling a law practice or area of law practice, including goodwill; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.17, with USPTO modification that a practice involving patent proceedings before the Office may be sold only to one or more registered practitioners or law firms that include at least one registered practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds USPTO-specific limitation to preserve competence/authorization to practice before the Office; governs transfer of client files and trust account records on sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties to prospective clients (§ 11.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule addressing a practitioner's responsibilities to prospective clients, corresponding to ABA Model Rule 1.18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers duties arising from initial communications and when confidentiality/conflicts obligations may attach to prospective-client interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of advice to client (§ 11.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule addressing the practitioner's role in providing advice to a client; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 2.1 but USPTO declines to enact the Model Rule's final sentence about referring to non-legal factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although USPTO omits that sentence, it does not prohibit practitioners from referring to moral, economic, social, or political considerations relevant to the client; clarifies permissible scope of non-legal considerations in advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation for third parties and disclosure obligations (§ 11.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical standards when a practitioner provides an evaluation of a matter affecting a client for use by a third party; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 2.3 and requires disclosure in compliance with duty of disclosure provisions of this subchapter and § 11.106(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing evaluations for third parties, practitioners must adhere to USPTO disclosure rules and may have obligations to disclose evaluation information to the Office as required by § 11.106(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party neutral service (§ 11.204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule addressing a practitioner's role in serving as a third-party neutral (arbitrator, mediator, etc.), corresponding to ABA Model Rule 2.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies ethical considerations and impartiality expectations for practitioners acting as neutrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meritorious claims and use of legal procedure (§ 11.301)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must present well-grounded positions and has a duty to use legal procedure for the fullest benefit of the client's cause, but not to abuse legal procedure; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.1, with USPTO deletion of certain criminal-law-specific language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits frivolous claims or contentions; USPTO excludes ABA's criminal-defense-specific phrasing about requiring every element be established because it is limited to criminal practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence and expediting proceedings (§ 11.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must diligently pursue litigation and Office proceedings and make reasonable efforts to expedite proceedings before the Office as well as in litigated matters; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.2 with USPTO emphasis on Office proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes affirmative obligation to move cases efficiently through USPTO processes in addition to general diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor to tribunal and duty to disclose adverse authority (§ 11.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued duty of candor with specific application: a practitioner must disclose legal authority in the controlling jurisdiction known to be directly adverse to the client's position and not disclosed by opposing counsel in inter partes proceedings, and must disclose such authority in ex parte proceedings before the Office where not otherwise disclosed; § 11.303(e) also specifies disclosure necessary to comply with the duty of disclosure provisions of this subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many USPTO decisions are ex parte and affect public interest, practitioners must cite known directly adverse authority to the Office in good faith; ABA references to criminal testimony are omitted as inapplicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair marshaling and presentation of evidence (§ 11.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must marshal evidence fairly in any case before a tribunal, including ex parte and inter partes proceedings before the Office; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies duties extend beyond trial to all tribunal proceedings; prohibits withholding, distorting, or improperly influencing evidence presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality, decorum, and prohibition on improper influence (§ 11.305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must act with impartiality and decorum in ex parte and inter partes proceedings and must not improperly influence hearing officers, administrative law judges, administrative patent judges, administrative trademark judges, employees, or officers of the Office; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.305(c) reserved re juror communications; practitioners who improperly communicate with jurors are subject to criminal law and state/court disciplinary rules and may face reciprocal USPTO action; lack of a specific USPTO rule does not imply conduct is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial publicity and related conduct (§ 11.306) — reserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Section is reserved because USPTO declines to enact a specific rule regarding trial publicity; however, improper conduct relating to trial publicity remains subject to disciplinary rules of appropriate State and Court authorities and may lead to USPTO action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even without a USPTO-specific rule, practitioners engaging in improper trial publicity can be disciplined by other authorities and face reciprocal USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate-witness rule (§ 11.307)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner is generally prohibited from acting as an advocate in a proceeding before the Office in which the practitioner is likely to be a necessary witness; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining advocate and witness roles can prejudice opposing parties and create conflicts of interest between client and practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct in non-adjudicative administrative proceedings (§ 11.309)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regulating a practitioner's conduct when representing a client in a non-adjudicative proceeding before an administrative agency, such as the Office; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailors obligations for situations where the proceeding is not adjudicative but the practitioner still has professional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness in communications on client's behalf (§ 11.401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must be truthful when dealing with others on a client's behalf; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 4.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits making false statements of material fact or law and limits use of partial truths that are misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating with represented parties and government contacts (§ 11.402(a)–(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: § 11.402(a) corresponds to MRPC 4.2 but adds that a practitioner may communicate with a represented party when authorized by law, court order, or rule; § 11.402(b) (based on D.C. Rule 4.2(b)) permits communications with certain government decision-makers without opposing counsel's consent under specified disclosures, but not to bypass government counsel on routine matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited direct contact with government decision makers to address genuine grievances (not routine discovery or scheduling); requires practitioners to make required disclosures when communicating with government employees who have remedial authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating with unrepresented persons (§ 11.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard for communicating with an unrepresented person, particularly one not experienced in legal matters; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 4.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must not give legal advice to unrepresented persons that would create a client-lawyer relationship and must clarify their role and protect the unrepresented person's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respecting rights of third persons and inadvertent disclosures (§ 11.404)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must respect the rights of third parties; responsibility to a client does not permit disregarding third-party rights and provides guidance regarding receipt of inadvertently sent documents; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 4.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes protocols for how to handle inadvertently produced/confidential documents and balancing client advocacy with third-party rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner and supervisory responsibilities (§ 11.501)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets forth the responsibilities of a partner or supervisory practitioner; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 5.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes obligations on supervisors to ensure subordinate compliance with rules and to establish reasonable policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of subordinate practitioners (§ 11.502)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets forth ethical and professional responsibilities of subordinate practitioners; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 5.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subordinates must follow supervisors' decisions but remain bound by professional rules when a subordinate knows a supervisor's conduct is a clear violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision of non-practitioner assistants (§ 11.503)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies practitioner responsibilities in supervising non-practitioner assistants (secretaries, technical advisors, student associates, draftspersons, investigators, law student interns, paraprofessionals); corresponds to ABA Model Rule 5.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must ensure assistants' conduct comports with professional obligations and implement safeguards when delegating tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of professional independence and fee-sharing limits (§ 11.504)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protects professional independence by limiting sharing fees with non-practitioners; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 5.4, but § 11.504(a)(4) permits sharing legal fees with certain nonprofit organizations (IRS 501(c)(3)) under stated conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows fee contributions to nonprofit organizations that employed/retained/recommended the practitioner and permits sharing to promote public-interest missions; requires practitioner to retain sole professional judgment; exception not limited to court-awarded fees to avoid interfering with settlements, but applies only to qualifying nonprofits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unauthorized practice and related restrictions (§ 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in or aiding the unauthorized practice of law (corresponds to MRPC 5.5(a)) and includes multiple USPTO-specific provisions: prohibits practice before the Office by practitioners suspended/excluded/inactive/administratively suspended or transferred to disability; prohibits assisting non-bar members or non-registered persons in unauthorized practice before the Office; prohibits aiding suspended/excluded practitioners in practice before the Office or other jurisdictions; recognizes pre-1957 non-attorney trademark agents' continued recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to protect public from unqualified providers; notes USPTO registers individuals not firms; gives examples and cites case law where attorneys aided unauthorized practice; clarifies sanctions and conduct that will be treated as unauthorized assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific prohibitions related to practice status (§ 11.505(b)–(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: § 11.505(b) bars practice before the Office if practitioner is suspended, excluded, transferred to disability inactive, administratively suspended, or inactive; § 11.505(c) bars assisting non-bar or non-registered persons in unauthorized practice before the Office; § 11.505(d) bars aiding suspended or excluded practitioners in practice before the Office; § 11.505(e) bars aiding suspended/excluded practitioners in other jurisdictions; § 11.505(f) recognizes certain pre-1957 trademark agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaks down the specific statuses and types of assistance that are prohibited and clarifies the limited exception for historically-recognized trademark agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on agreements restricting rights to practice (§ 11.506)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner is prohibited from entering agreements that restrict the practitioner's right to practice, corresponding to ABA Model Rule 5.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents contractual arrangements that limit lawyers' ability to provide future legal services or to practice law freely as part of settlement or employment arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to law-related services (§ 11.507)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner providing law-related services is subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 5.7 and relies on the definition of 'law-related service' in § 11.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends professional responsibility to services reasonably related to the practice of law before the Office even if not strictly legal services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and advertising about services (§§ 11.701–11.704)
rubrics_metrics.description: § 11.701 governs all communications about practitioner services (corresponding to MRPC 7.1); § 11.702 addresses advertising (MRPC 7.2) but declines to adopt MRPC 7.2(b)(2) regarding regulation of lawyer referral services; § 11.703 addresses direct contact with prospective clients (MRPC 7.3); § 11.704 permits indicating areas of practice and includes designations relating to limited recognition (§ 11.704(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets boundaries on truthful advertising, permissible solicitations, how to identify practice areas, and how practitioners with limited recognition may label themselves. USPTO declines to regulate lawyer referral services and certain specialization communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm names and letterhead (§ 11.705)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulates firm names and letterheads corresponding to ABA Model Rule 7.5; some subsections reserved or declined (e.g., 11.705(b) reserved, 11.705(d) declined), but improper use remains subject to state/court disciplinary rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must not misrepresent firm structure or imply associations not factually accurate; absence of USPTO-specific rule does not permit misleading firm name practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty in admissions and registration (§ 11.801)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposes the same duty to persons seeking admission to a bar and to practitioners seeking registration or limited recognition (corresponding to MRPC 8.1), including that material false statements in connection with registration/recognition can be basis for discipline and requires cooperation with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applicants and practitioners; knowingly making misrepresentations in disciplinary investigations or failing to clarify misunderstandings with admissions authorities is misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false statements about judges and public legal officers (§ 11.802)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not make statements known to be false or with reckless disregard for truth concerning the qualifications or integrity of a judge, adjudicatory officer, public legal officer, or candidate for such office; corresponds to MRPC 8.2 and recognizes USPTO employees as adjudicatory officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers attacks on integrity/qualifications of USPTO adjudicators (administrative patent judges, examiners, etc.) and aims to protect the fairness and integrity of adjudicative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to report professional misconduct (§ 11.803)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires reporting violations of the Rules of Professional Conduct (corresponds to MRPC 8.3), but reporting may not be required where it would violate § 11.106(a); practitioners should encourage client consent to disclosure when prosecution would not prejudice client; § 11.803(c) does not require disclosure of information protected by § 11.106 or information gained in approved lawyers assistance programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances obligation to report with duty of confidentiality and protections for certain assistance programs; explains limits and exceptions to reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct definitions and sanctionable conduct (§ 11.804)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section addresses misconduct (corresponding to MRPC 8.4(a)–(f)) and does not attempt an exhaustive list; § 11.804(g) addresses knowing assistance to an Office officer/employee in violating rules or law; § 11.804(h) states being publicly disciplined on ethical grounds by a State/US/foreign authority is misconduct; § 11.804(i) states conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice before the Office is misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies categories of sanctionable behavior, warns that absence of specific examples does not imply permissibility of certain acts previously listed in older rules, and clarifies special instances (assisting Office employees in misconduct; public discipline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Savings clauses for disciplinary proceedings (§ 11.901)
rubrics_metrics.description: Savings clauses providing (a) disciplinary proceedings may be instituted after effective date for conduct engaged in prior to the effective date if such conduct would continue to justify sanctions under the new part; (b) no practitioner shall be subject to discipline under this part for prior conduct if such conduct would not have been subject to disciplinary action before the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition rule clarifying retroactivity and non-retroactivity limits for disciplinary actions when the new rules take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference table of principal sources for §§ 11.101–11.804 (Table 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mapping that identifies the principal source (MRPC, USPTO, DCRPR, etc.) for each listed section (e.g., § 11.101 = MRPC 1.1; § 11.115(f)(1) = MRCTAR Rule 1; § 11.303 = MRPC 3.3, USPTO), showing how USPTO provisions relate to ABA Model Rules and other authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for determining which provisions are verbatim from Model Rules, which are USPTO-specific, and where D.C. or other rules informed USPTO modifications; the table enumerates the principal sources for each section covered.
